subject.title: bug(telegram): reply to bot photo injects bot-sent media as inbound user attachment

question: Should Telegram reply-chain hydration include media from bot-authored reply targets when visibility allows it, or should those media fetches be skipped as self-authored re-ingestion?
rationale: Current source can reproduce the reported media fetch, but current tests and a closed related PR treat the same bot-authored media as intentional context, so automation cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Confirm current hydration contract
options.body: Treat bot-authored reply media as load-bearing conversation context and close this issue plus the conflicting cross-fork PR with the current tests and prior discussion cited.

options.title: Adopt a self-authored media skip
options.body: Change `resolveReplyMediaForChain` to skip bot-authored media fetches, update focused bot- and user-authored reply-media tests, and require redacted Telegram after-fix proof.

options.title: Narrow the distinction
options.body: Preserve bot-authored media in visible reply-chain context but prevent it from being presented as current inbound user media if a narrower duplicate-injection path still exists.

recommendation.title: Confirm current hydration contract
recommendation.body: Treat bot-authored reply media as load-bearing conversation context and close this issue plus the conflicting cross-fork PR with the current tests and prior discussion cited.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and merged the most recent visibility-aware reply-media hydration changes and have the clearest current-history context for the contract.
